The Curvature of a Joint Score-Driven Filter

Source: R/gas_joint_core.R
term_curvature.GasJoint.Rd

Computes the Jacobian of every filtered predictor in a caller's unknowns and the second derivative of the filtered predictors contracted against the caller's weights, propagated through the joint recursion.

Arguments

term

A GasJoint().

eta, y, score, curvature

Unused: the recursion reads the data in blocks. They are kept for the signature of the generic.

psi

The terms' parameters, as for term_filter().

g

The weights, a matrix with one column per filtered parameter.

seed

A list with one matrix per distribution parameter: the derivative of that equation's static predictor in the unknowns, one row per observation. The joint filter's parameters are the last columns, in the order of term_params().

blocks

A list with filtered (the position in seed of the equation of each filtered parameter), u (the driving scores at the fitted predictors, a matrix with one column per filtered parameter), U1 and U2 (the first and second derivatives of each driving score in every predictor, arrays of dimension c(n, K, P) and c(n, K, P, P)), and, for the third and fourth orders, U3 and U4, with one more dimension of length P each.

...

Unused.

Value

A list with jacobian (one matrix per filtered parameter) and curvature.

Details

The level of each parameter and each driving score are carried as jets: a value with its derivatives. The jet of a level is a sum of products of the chart's jets with the jets of earlier driving scores and levels, and the jet of a driving score at a row is formed from the jets of the predictors of every equation by the chain rule, with the driving score's derivatives in those predictors supplied as data in blocks. The static rows of every equation enter through seed, and only a filtered equation's predictor has a second derivative.
